t: Notwithstanding section 5 of the Animal Drug User Fee Act of 2003 (21 U.S.C. 379j–11 note), and notwithstanding the amendments made by this title, part 4 of subchapter C of chapter VII of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 379j–11 et seq.), as in effect on the day before the date of the enactment of this title, shall continue to be in effect with respect to animal drug applications and supplemental animal drug applications (as defined in such part as of such day) that on or after September 1, 2003, but before October 1, 2008, were accepted by the Food and Drug Administration for filing with respect to assessing and collecting any fee required by such part for a fiscal year prior to fiscal year 2009.

fable.w: This is a savings clause that keeps the prior user-fee provisions in effect for animal drug applications accepted for filing before October 1, 2008, for purposes of assessing and collecting fees. The tempting reading is that companies filing applications with the FDA are interacting with a federal decision, but applications are expressly excluded from participation. Nothing in the section provides for consultation, comment, hearings, an advisory body, or a right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: shall continue to be in effect with respect to animal drug applications and supplemental animal drug applications

opus.w: This is a savings clause. It keeps the old animal drug user fee rules in effect for applications accepted between 2003 and 2008, for fees owed for years before fiscal year 2009. No outside party is consulted, there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or advisory body, and no right to sue is created. The mention of drug applications does not count, because the DEFINITION says applications are not participation.
opus.s: shall continue to be in effect with respect to animal drug applications and supplemental animal drug applications
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions animal drug applications "accepted by the Food and Drug Administration for filing," which might look like outsiders interacting with an agency. That reading fails because the DEFINITION excludes applications, and this provision only says which version of the fee law applies to them. No one outside the federal government is consulted, no comment period or hearing is required, and no right to sue is granted.

qwen_chat.w: This section dictates which fee regulations apply to animal drug applications already accepted for filing. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a federal decision is made. The interaction described is the submission of an application, which the definition explicitly excludes from participation.
qwen_chat.s: part 4 of subchapter C of chapter VII of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 379j–11 et seq.), as in effect on the day before the date of the enactment of this title, shall continue to be in effect with respect to animal drug applications and supplemental animal drug applications... that on or after September 1, 2003, but before October 1, 2008, were accepted by the Food and Drug Administration for filing with respect to assessing and collecting any fee
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section mentions "animal drug applications," it involves outside parties (companies) interacting with the government. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses" are not participation. Furthermore, this section is purely about the applicability of fee structures to applications already filed; it does not create a new process for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties before a decision is made. It is a procedural/financial provision regarding existing filings.
